# S22 — Import from ADR folders

Add adj import-adr DIR: read an ADR folder in the Nygard (adr-tools) or MADR format and create one adj record per ADR, so a team that keeps ADRs can move to adj with its history.

**Findings:** PROJECT.md Feature tiers (Later) · **Size:** L · **Tree:** cli

**2026-10-16** — From S25 review: imported (ADR) record files will often not be in the form model.Marshal writes (empty arrays, no final newline in the body). C163 compares stale copies as stored for that reason; keep any importer or new comparison on the same footing.

[--by NAME] [--dry-run] [--root DIR]'; DIR is positional, relative DIR is taken from the working directory, and DIR must be inside the repo root, because each record's file ref is the file's slash path relative to the root. reason: the slice asks for refs relative to the repo root and a folder outside it has no such path; --dry-run adopted because an import is bulk and the owner wants to see warnings before writing.

One entry per imported record: date = run date, note = 'from FILE' (path from the repo root). No fake ask/decide entries. reason: the record's created/decided_at come from the ADR date, and an ask/decide entry dated the run would claim adj asked and decided it. Changes the set of valid event values, so an older adj would reject a store with imported records; the owner should confirm.

**2026-10-18** — C32 decision (S22, status mapping): the first word of the status text, in any case and ignoring markup, bullets and trailing punctuation: accepted -> decided, proposed -> open, rejected -> rejected, deprecated -> withdrawn, superseded -> superseded. A line 'Superseded by ...' wins over an earlier 'Accepted'; 'Supersedes ...', 'Amended by ...' lines are ignored. Any other word, or no status, is an error naming the file (no guessing). reason: the slice names these words; guessing a status for an unknown word would put a wrong decision in the log.

**2026-10-18** — C32 decision (S22, identity and order): ADR numbers are not kept as IDs. Records take the next free IDs, created in ADR number order (the N. of an adr-tools title, else the leading digits of the file name, then the file name), not plain file-name order, so 10-x.md comes after 2-y.md. Each record has refs [FILE path from the root, ADR-NNNN] (the second only when the number is above 0; an ADR numbered 0000 counts as unnumbered). A file is already imported when any record has its path as a ref; skipped files are not parsed and not linked. Only .md files directly in DIR whose names start with a number (optional adr-/adr_) are ADRs; README.md, templates and subfolders are ignored silently. reason: IDs should follow decision order; refs make the second run idempotent and keep the ADR number findable with adj list/check --ref.

**2026-10-18** — C32 decision (S22, supersede links): a superseded ADR is linked only to a target in the same run, found by the file name in its link, else by a number that exactly one ADR has, and only if the target is accepted or itself superseded and no loop results. Otherwise (no target named, target not in the run, ambiguous number, itself, target proposed/rejected/deprecated, cycle) the record is imported as decided and a warning says why, as the slice recommends. Links come from the 'Superseded by' side only; 'Supersedes' lines are not read. Write order: every record is created first (a superseded one as decided, no links), then for each link the old record is updated first and the new one second, as adj supersede does (C136), so a failure between leaves the decision in force intact. reason: Create assigns the IDs, so links can only be written after all records exist.

**2026-10-18** — C32 decision (S22, field mapping): decided: decision = Decision section (MADR: the label in 'Chosen option: "X"', else the Decision Outcome text); rationale = first non-blank of MADR justification (text after 'because'), Consequences, Context; the Consequences section also goes to the consequences field unless the rationale already is that text. rejected/withdrawn: no decision; rationale chain starts with justification, then the Decision text ('we will not ...'), Consequences, Context. open: decision text becomes the recommendation (label when it equals a Considered Option, else text), reasoning = justification else Consequences; no rationale. Options = MADR Considered Options top-level bullets (links reduced to their text, repeats once), label only. accepted ADR with no decision, or answered ADR with none of the rationale sources, is an error naming the file; every file is checked before the first write. created/decided_at = ADR date (YYYY-MM-DD, a timestamp's date part is taken); no or invalid date -> run date plus a warning. No key, no body, no tags except --tag. reason: slice says rationale = Consequences or the MADR justification; the fallbacks avoid inventing text and avoid losing the ADR's content.

**2026-10-18** — C32 decision (S22, fix round 1, overrules the 'identity and order' note on skipping): a file is already imported only when a record has an import history entry whose note is 'from FILE' (the slash path from the root). A record whose refs hold the path, such as one asked by hand with --ref, does not cause a skip. Skipped files are now read again, only for their 'Superseded by' line (a file that no longer parses is ignored, never an error). An ADR file that is a symbolic link is not read: a warning 'FILE: symbolic link skipped' (only for names that look like ADRs). reason: a ref is an opaque string anyone can add, so matching on it could silently drop an ADR; the import entry is written only by import.

## Why

Listed in the Later tier (PROJECT.md). Owner decision 2026-10-18: keep it, with adj import-adr DIR supporting both common formats: Michael Nygard's template as written by adr-tools ("# N. Title", "Date: YYYY-MM-DD", ## Status / ## Context / ## Decision / ## Consequences) and MADR (optional YAML front matter with status and date, or a "Status:"/"Date:" line; # Title; ## Context and Problem Statement, ## Considered Options, ## Decision Outcome). Earlier note (S25 review): imported files are not in model.Marshal's form; C163 compares stale copies as stored, so keep any new comparison on that footing.

## Failing tests

Red first, table-driven, fixtures in testdata, stores in t.TempDir():
- Each fixture parses to the expected title (adr-tools' 'N. ' prefix stripped), status, date, context, decision text and option list (MADR Considered Options).
- Mapping: accepted -> decided (decision = Decision section text via the --text path, rationale = Consequences or MADR outcome justification), proposed -> open, rejected -> rejected, deprecated -> withdrawn, superseded -> superseded with superseded_by/supersedes links when the target ADR is in the same import (by its number), otherwise decided-then-superseded is not possible: decide under C32 (recommend: import as decided and list a warning).
- created and decided_at come from the ADR date; a missing date uses the run date and is reported.
- Each record gets a ref naming the source file (path relative to the repo root) so a second import of the same folder skips files already imported (exit 0, reported) instead of duplicating.
- adj lint is clean on the resulting store for every fixture set.
- --dry-run (if adopted under C32) writes nothing and prints what would be created.
- A DIR with no ADR files exits 0 printing nothing; an unreadable file or unparseable required part exits 1 naming the file and writes nothing for any file (validate all first, then write).
- Usage errors exit 2.

1. Decide under C32 and record as slicer notes on S22 (recommendations in brackets): command name and flags [adj import-adr DIR [--tag T]... [--by NAME] [--dry-run]]; history [one new 'import' event with note 'from FILE' instead of faking ask/decide entries; add it to model.Event, Valid, docs/json.md, and lint if lint checks events]; decided_by [--by, else $ADJ_DECIDED_BY, else blank: lint's decided-by warning then applies, which is honest]; asked_by [blank or the ADR's deciders field if MADR has one]; status words matched case-insensitively with the first word of the Status section; ADR numbers are not kept as IDs (records take the next free IDs) but are kept as a ref like ADR-0007 so supersede links can be resolved.

3. Validate every file before writing any record; write in ADR-number order so supersede targets exist when linked (or link in a second pass under the lock).
